name: Slovak Republic
headline: Slovak Republic: +0.8% growth in 2025, 4.2% inflation, debt 61% of GDP
sections: Slovak Republic is a $154 billion economy (2025), the world's 61st-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +0.8% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $49K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 16.2% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 4.2% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 12.1% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 5.4% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 18.4% (2025).
Gross government debt is 61% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has risen from 58% in 2020. The general government balance is −4.5% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −3.6% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 170% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 72% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 78.4 years (2024). Population: 5.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
